subject.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload

question: Should OpenClaw expose a gateway-drain bypass through plugin-visible queue APIs, or must this restart-drain admission path stay entirely core-internal before this PR can merge?
rationale: The branch changes a public/plugin-visible SDK contract in a way that can bypass shutdown admission; automation cannot decide whether that is an intentional plugin API/security boundary.

options.title: Keep The Bypass Core-Internal
options.body: Remove plugin-visible enqueueInternal/drain-bypass surface and preserve the SIGUSR1 drain behavior through private core-owned plumbing, then require exact-head proof.

options.title: Approve A Public SDK Contract
options.body: Allow the new bypass only with maintainer-approved docs, compatibility tests, and security guidance that define when plugins may use it.

options.title: Defer To Durable Recovery
options.body: Pause this in-memory mitigation and route the central restart message-loss work to the SQLite-backed recovery PR or a successor design.

recommendation.title: Keep The Bypass Core-Internal
recommendation.body: Remove plugin-visible enqueueInternal/drain-bypass surface and preserve the SIGUSR1 drain behavior through private core-owned plumbing, then require exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the plugin SDK queue contract, and steipete has the strongest recent history on that shared queue surface plus adjacent followup queue lifecycle work.
